Omri. Twelve years; the founder of Samaria.

ISRAEL (THE NORTH): 19 RULERS JEROBOAM I → HOSHEA
ACCESSION
How Omri came to power
When Zimri killed Elah, “all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp” at Gibbethon. 1 Kings 16:16
The people then split: half followed Tibni son of Ginath, half followed Omri; Omri's side prevailed, “so Tibni died, and Omri reigned”. 1 Kings 16:21–22

The two kingdoms

BUT ALSO
Micah later names his rule as a pattern: “the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab”. Micah 6:16

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
THIELE, AS REVISED BY MCFALL AND YOUNG
Shared rule with Tibni (rival king), 885–880 BC
Rival king from 885/884 BC, sole king from 880, died 874/873
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 876–869 (p. 20); 8 years against the Hebrew text's 12 (last digit partly lost in the scan's gutter, read from the next reign's start).
TRADITIONAL (USSHER, 1658)
Shared rule with Tibni (rival king), 929–925 BC
Chosen by the army in the year of the world 3075; reigns alone from 3079 (925 BC); dies 3086 (Annals, p. 45)
From the camp at Gibbethon, with a rival reign
R. C. Young's tables (Thiele as revised)
Young counts Omri from 885/884 BC, when the army made him king, with Tibni as a rival until 880; Asa's thirty-first year (1 Kings 16:23) then marks the start of his sole reign.[1]
From the camp, sole rule four years later
James Ussher, Annals of the World (1658), p. 45
Ussher has Omri chosen in the year of the world 3075 (929 BC) and beginning “to reign over Israel alone in the 31 year of king Asa”, 925 BC, after Tibni.[2]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
1 Kings 16 2 Kings 8 2 Chronicles 22 Micah 6
PASSAGES · 4
1 Kings 16:15–28 2 Kings 8:26 2 Chronicles 22:2 Micah 6:16
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture names no father, tribe or mother for Omri, and says nothing of his wars.
Kings mentions “his might that he shewed” but leaves the details to “the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel”.
The Bible does not mention his conquest of Moab; that comes from the Mesha Stele.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
“Omri, the captain of the host” — Scripture names no father or tribe for him. 1 Kings 16:16
